## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical dependency security skills in a real monorepo environment containing both JavaScript and Python services, along with understanding of license compliance policies.

## Key Concepts
- Integrating npm audit and pip-audit into CI pipelines
- Lightweight license allowlist enforcement
- Building a CI gate that blocks merges on CVEs or disallowed licenses
- Verification workflows for both local development and CI environments

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/dependency-security.yml
name: Dependency Security Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  security-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      
      - name: Install Node dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Run npm audit
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high
      
      - name: Run pip-audit
        run: pip-audit -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Check licenses
        run: |
          npx license-checker --json > licenses.json
          # Script checks licenses against allowlist
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of policy-as-code and practical gate setup for Kubernetes manifests. It targets beginners learning to automate policy checks.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext
- Conftest and Rego
- CI integration for policy gates
- Manifest validation

## Code Example
```rego
package conftest.policy

# Deny hostNetwork/hostPID
deny[reason] {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  input.spec.hostNetwork == true
  reason = "hostNetwork must be disabled"
}
deny[reason] {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  input.spec.hostPID == true
  reason = "hostPID must be disabled"
}
# RunAsNonRoot checks for containers
deny[reason] {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  c := input.spec.containers[_]
  not c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  reason = "containers must set runAsNonRoot: true"
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to create simple, deterministic CI gates focused on security hygiene in manifests, with minimal tooling. Shows understanding of Kubernetes volumes, YAML parsing, and CI integration.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes hostPath security risks
- Manifest scanning with lightweight parsers (yq, Python)
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- Local verification of a detector script

## Code Example

```python
# detector.py
import sys, yaml
def has_hostpath(path):
  data = yaml.safe_load(open(path))
  vols = data.get('spec', {}).get('volumes', []) or []
  for v in vols:
    if 'hostPath' in v:
      return True
  return False
if __name__ == '__main__':
  ok = True
  for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    if has_hostpath(f):
      ok = False
      print('HOSTPATH found in', f)
  sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question demonstrates end-to-end supply chain security expertise: image signing, SBOM provenance tracking, CVE scanning, and runtime verification in a multi-cloud, high-stakes environment. It tests knowledge of Sigstore ecosystem tools and policy enforcement.

- Image signing with Cosign/Sigstore for supply chain integrity
- CycloneDX SBOM generation for component transparency
- CVE scanning integration (e.g., Trivy, Snyk) for vulnerability detection
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy for runtime enforcement
- Canary deployments and rollback strategies in multi-cloud contexts

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`)
```yaml
name: Image Provenance Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-scan-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate CycloneDX SBOM
        uses: cyclonedx/ghcr-create-sbom@v1
        with:
          format: json
          output-file: sbom.json
      
      - name: Run CVE scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: json
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
      
      - name: Sign image with Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-version: 'v2'
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft ghcr.io/org/app:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```

### Gatekeeper Policy (`constraint-template.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: requirecosignsignature
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RequireCosignSignature
      targets:
        - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
          rego: |
            package requirecosignsignature
            violation["image is not signed with Cosign"] {
              image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
              notcosign.verify(image)
            }
```

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: unsigned-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:unsigned-latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

### Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-app
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
```

# Verify image signature
cosign verify ghcr.io/org/app:v1.0.0

# Verify SBOM exists

deny[msg]{
  input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
  some i
  input.review.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i].hostPath
  not hasAnnotation(input.review.object.metadata.namespace, "devsecops.enabled", "true")
  msg = "HostPath mounts are restricted unless devsecops.enabled=true"
}
